title: NI Water submits its PC28 business plan
detail: NI Water's business plan for the 2028–2033 price control goes to the Utility Regulator. It sets out what NI Water says it needs for water and wastewater, including the capacity that decides where new homes and premises can connect.
sectors: Councils; Construction and developers; Water customers
action: Councils and developers: note what the plan says about wastewater capacity in the places you need connections, ready for the draft determination in June 2027.
source_title: Decision published on approach to PC28, NI Water's next price control (Utility Regulator)
note: The Utility Regulator gives the month, not a day.

title: Withdrawal Agreement Joint Committee meets
detail: The UK has said it intends to agree at this meeting to add the EU Forced Labour Regulation (EU) 2024/3015 to the Windsor Framework, so that it would apply in Northern Ireland from 14 December 2027 (Article 36 excluded), subject to the Assembly's democratic scrutiny safeguards.
action: Watch for the decision text. If the regulation is added, start mapping forced-labour risk in the supply chains behind goods you place on the NI market.
source_title: Explanatory memorandum on Regulation (EU) 2024/3015 (UK Government, 4 November 2026)

title: UK–EU summit in Brussels
detail: The second UK–EU summit. Draft texts reported by the press would conclude talks on linking the UK and EU emissions trading systems, with each side's goods exempt from the other's carbon border levy, and on an agri-food (SPS) agreement. None of this is confirmed, and nothing changes for either CBAM until both sides legislate.
sectors: Manufacturers; Importers; Exporters to the EU; Food and drink; Farmers
action: Plan on both CBAMs applying as they stand. Read the summit statement for any link start date and for how goods moving GB to NI would be treated.
source_title: Prime Minister to attend UK–EU summit in Brussels on 20 November (GOV.UK, 12 October 2026)
note: The summit date is confirmed by GOV.UK. The ETS link and SPS outcomes are reported from draft texts (Euronews, 6 November 2026), not confirmed.

title: Plastic waste exports to non-OECD countries banned
detail: Under the EU Waste Shipments Regulation (EU) 2024/1157, which applies in Northern Ireland, plastic waste can no longer be exported to countries outside the OECD, at least until 21 May 2029.
action: Ask your waste contractor or broker where your plastic waste goes and get it in writing. Councils: check the end destinations in your recycling contracts.
source_title: Plastic waste shipments (European Commission)

title: ECHA's final opinion on the universal PFAS restriction due
detail: ECHA plans to send its final opinion on restricting PFAS across the EU to the European Commission later in 2026 and at the latest by the end of 2026. The Commission and member states then decide in 2027. Any restriction would apply in NI through EU REACH.
sectors: Manufacturers; Chemicals; Construction and developers; Retail and hospitality
action: List the PFAS uses in your products and processes (coatings, seals, foams, fluoropolymers) and ask suppliers which they can replace.
source_title: Next steps in ECHA's assessment of the universal PFAS restriction (ECHA presentation, EMA, 4 February 2026)
note: Timetable as published in February 2026; ECHA may move it.

title: New EU product liability rules apply to products placed on the NI market
detail: The Product Liability Directive (EU) 2024/2853 applies to products placed on the NI market or put into service on or after 9 December 2026. It brings software, digital files and online sellers within strict liability for defective products.
action: Check your product liability insurance and supply contracts cover products sold into NI from this date, including any software or connected features.
source_title: Explanatory memorandum on Directive (EU) 2024/2853 (Department for Business and Trade, via the NI Assembly)

title: DfE biomethane strategy consultation closes
detail: Department for the Economy consultation on a Biomethane Strategy and Policy Framework for NI, covering energy and agricultural resilience, nutrient management and decarbonisation. Closes at 5pm.
sectors: Farmers; Energy and renewables; Food and drink; Energy users
action: If you produce slurry, digestate or food waste, or use gas, respond before 5pm on 15 December.
source_title: Biomethane Strategy and Policy Framework consultation (Department for the Economy)
note: Closing date as recorded in the NI Consultations Monitor (checked on the DfE page, 6 November 2026) and in published coverage of the consultation.

title: EU deforestation rules apply in NI to medium and large firms, and to all firms placing wood products
detail: The EU Deforestation Regulation applies in NI from 30 December 2026 to medium and large operators, and to micro and small operators of products already under the EU Timber Regulation. Covers cattle, cocoa, coffee, palm oil, rubber, soya and wood. DAERA enforces for cattle, cocoa, coffee, palm oil and soy; OPSS for wood and rubber.
sectors: Food and drink; Construction and developers; Retail and hospitality; Importers
action: First placers on the NI market: collect plot geolocation from suppliers and file due diligence statements before goods are placed after 30 December.
source_title: Moving, exporting or placing deforestation-free products on the market in Northern Ireland (GOV.UK, updated 27 August 2026)

title: ESOS phase 4 qualification date
detail: An undertaking is in ESOS phase 4 if on 31 December 2026 it, or its UK group, employs 250 or more people, or has turnover above £44m and a balance sheet above £38m. NIEA regulates organisations registered in NI.
action: Check headcount and group accounts as at 31 December. If you qualify, appoint a lead assessor early and pick a 12-month reference period ending before 5 December 2027.
source_title: How to comply with ESOS phase 4 (GOV.UK, published 30 July 2026)

title: First quarterly UK CBAM rates published
detail: The government calculates and publishes UK CBAM rates at the beginning of each quarter from 1 January 2027, so the next ones follow in April, July and October 2027.
action: Reprice 2027 import budgets and customer quotes using the published rate for your goods.
source_title: Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism: policy summary (HMRC, updated 2 November 2026)

title: Digital waste tracking becomes mandatory for NI receiving sites
detail: Transfer stations, scrap yards, landfills, energy-from-waste plants and composting sites in NI must record the waste they receive on the UK digital waste tracking service. England and Wales started in October 2026.
action: Receiving sites: join the public beta now and test your weighbridge and software links before January.
source_title: Digital waste tracking (NetRegs, for NIEA and SEPA)
note: Marked expected because the NI regulations were not yet made on 9 November 2026. GOV.UK's service page (updated 1 October 2026) also gives January 2027 for NI.

title: UK CBAM starts
detail: The UK carbon border levy applies across the UK, NI included, to imported aluminium, cement, fertiliser, hydrogen, iron and steel of any non-UK origin, EU included: HMRC says no jurisdiction is currently exempt. Liability starts once covered imports pass £50,000 in any 12 months. Charged on direct emissions, using global default values in 2027 and 2028 where supplier data is missing.
sectors: Importers; Manufacturers; Construction and developers; Farmers
action: From 1 January keep a record for every covered import: commodity code, origin, mass, value and the supplier's emissions data, and track the £50,000 test monthly.
source_title: Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism: policy summary (HMRC, updated 2 November 2026)
note: Default values from Budget 2026 (HC 726, para 6.217): global in 2027 and 2028, country-specific from 2029.

title: EU F-gas bans on new cooling and heat pump kit; HFC supply halves
detail: Under the EU F-gas Regulation (EU) 2024/573, which applies in NI, these can no longer be placed on the market: plug-in and other self-contained air conditioning and heat pumps up to 50 kW with refrigerant GWP 150 or more; split air-to-water heat pumps up to 12 kW with GWP 150 or more; chillers up to 12 kW with GWP 150 or more and above 12 kW with GWP 750 or more (safety exceptions apply). The EU's maximum HFC quantity falls from 42.9 to 21.7 million tonnes CO2e a year for 2027–2029. Great Britain keeps its own rules.
sectors: Retail and hospitality; Food and drink; Construction and developers; Installers
action: Specify low-GWP refrigerants for any cooling or heat pump kit bought for NI sites, and budget for dearer HFC servicing gas.
source_title: Regulation (EU) 2024/573 on fluorinated greenhouse gases, Annexes IV and VII (EUR-Lex)
note: Kit placed on the market before 1 January 2027 can still be installed and serviced.

title: Listed companies report against UK Sustainability Reporting Standards
detail: FCA rules require listed companies to report against the UK SRS on a comply-or-explain basis for accounting periods starting on or after 1 January 2027, with first reports in 2028. Their suppliers will be asked for emissions data.
action: Suppliers to listed firms: have a Scope 1 and 2 footprint and a product-level method ready for customer questionnaires.
source_title: PS26/19: Aligning listed issuers' sustainability disclosures with international standards (FCA, 30 September 2026)

title: EU publishes the Q4 2026 CBAM certificate price
detail: The European Commission publishes the last quarterly CBAM certificate price for 2026 imports. From 2027 it publishes weekly prices.
action: If you ship CBAM goods from GB or outside the EU direct to EU customers, use the price to settle who carries the 2026 cost.
source_title: Price of CBAM certificates (European Commission)
note: The EU CBAM does not apply in NI; goods dispatched from NI do not trigger it.

title: Consultation on fixed price certificates in the Renewables Obligation closes
detail: DESNZ proposes replacing tradable certificates in the UK-wide Renewables Obligation schemes with fixed price certificates, covering pricing, supplier levies, reconciliation and transition. Closes at 11:59pm.
action: NI Renewables Obligation generators: check how the proposals treat NIRO and respond by 12 January.
source_title: Proposed implementation of fixed price certificates into the UK-wide RO schemes (DESNZ, 3 November 2026)
note: The consultation page says UK-wide RO schemes but does not name NIRO; check the consultation document.

title: EU Machinery Regulation applies in NI
detail: Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 replaces the Machinery Directive in NI under the Windsor Framework. Delegated acts adding AI safety-component requirements follow from 2 August 2028. GB continues to recognise CE marking for machinery.
sectors: Manufacturers; Importers; Construction and developers; Farmers
action: Makers and importers: update technical files, instructions and declarations of conformity for machinery placed on the NI market from 20 January.
source_title: Assessment of impact on Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 amending the Machinery Regulation (DfE, via the NI Assembly)

title: Consultation on adding refinery products to UK CBAM closes
detail: HM Treasury and HMRC seek views on the feasibility and impacts of bringing refinery products into UK CBAM in future. No start date is proposed. Closes at 11:59pm.
sectors: Energy users; Importers; Transport and shipping
action: If you import fuels or other refinery products from outside the UK, respond with your volumes and costs by 20 January.
source_title: CBAM: a consultation on sectoral scope expansion to include refinery products (HM Treasury and HMRC, 28 October 2026)

title: FSA consultation on NI food contact materials rules closes
detail: The Food Standards Agency in NI proposes the Materials and Articles in Contact with Food Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2027, updating and consolidating enforcement of EU rules on plastics, recycled plastics, bisphenol A, and PFAS and heavy metals in food-contact packaging. Closes at 11:59pm.
sectors: Food and drink; Packaging producers; Retail and hospitality
action: Food businesses and packaging suppliers: check your declarations of compliance cover BPA and PFAS limits, and respond by 29 January.
source_title: Proposed update and consolidation of NI's domestic legislative framework for food contact materials (FSA, 5 November 2026)

title: EU CBAM certificates go on sale
detail: EU importers buy CBAM certificates on the common central platform from February 2027, starting with certificates for goods imported in 2026.
action: EU customers will want verified emissions data to cut their certificate bill: have product-level figures ready for anything you ship from GB or outside the EU.
source_title: Price of CBAM certificates (European Commission)
note: The Commission and the EPA (Ireland) give February 2027; the site's other dashboards use 1 February. The EU CBAM does not apply in NI.

title: Battery passports and removability rules start
detail: Under the EU Batteries Regulation, which applies in NI: each EV battery, light-means-of-transport battery and industrial battery above 2 kWh placed on the market needs a digital battery passport, and portable batteries must be removable and replaceable by the user. QR code labels on all batteries apply from this date at the earliest, subject to further legislation.
sectors: Manufacturers; Importers; Retail and hospitality; Transport and shipping
action: Battery and device makers and importers: confirm passport data and design changes with suppliers for stock reaching NI after 18 February.
source_title: EU batteries regulations in Northern Ireland (GOV.UK, updated 17 October 2026)
note: OPSS handles compliance queries; DAERA handles waste battery (Chapter 8) queries.

title: EU deadline to transpose the slimmed-down CSRD
detail: Member states must transpose the Omnibus I changes to the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive 12 months after the directive came into force (March 2027). In-scope EU groups now have more than 1,000 employees and over €450m turnover. CSRD is not in the Windsor Framework: NI firms are caught only through EU subsidiaries or EU turnover, or as suppliers.
sectors: Large businesses; Exporters to the EU; Manufacturers
action: If you have an EU subsidiary or large EU customers, confirm whether you are in scope under the new thresholds, and expect fewer but more targeted data requests.
source_title: Directive (EU) 2026/470 (Omnibus I), Official Journal, 26 February 2026 (EUR-Lex)
note: Transposition rule read in the adopted text (Council PE-CONS 66/25, Article 5). Published commentary gives 19 March 2027.

title: First UK ETS emissions reports for domestic shipping
detail: Ship operators in the UK ETS (domestic voyages from 1 July 2026, GB–NI sailings included) submit verified 2026 emissions reports.
action: Freight customers on GB–NI routes: ask your ferry operator how the carbon cost will appear on 2027 rates.
source_title: UK ETS scope expansion: domestic maritime, main Authority response (GOV.UK)

title: EU importers must hold CBAM certificates at each quarter end
detail: From 2027, authorised EU CBAM declarants must hold certificates covering at least 50% of the embedded emissions of goods imported since the start of the year at the end of each quarter.
action: Expect EU customers to ask for emissions data quarterly, not yearly, from 2027.
source_title: CBAM certificates (Environmental Protection Agency, Ireland)
note: The EPA is Ireland's CBAM competent authority. The first quarter end is 31 March 2027.

title: Simpler Recycling reaches micro-firms in England
detail: Workplaces in England with fewer than 10 full-time equivalent employees must separate recycling by 31 March 2027. It does not apply in NI.
sectors: Retail and hospitality; All businesses with sites in England
action: NI firms with small sites in England: arrange separate collections there before 31 March.
source_title: Simpler Recycling: workplace recycling in England (GOV.UK)
note: England only.

title: GB manufacturers exempted from some electricity levies; NI scheme funded but not dated
detail: Under the British Industrial Competitiveness Scheme, eligible businesses in Great Britain are exempted from the indirect costs of the Renewables Obligation and Feed-in Tariffs from 1 April 2027, with the Capacity Market to follow. The NI Executive is being funded to deliver a comparable scheme; no start date has been given.
action: NI manufacturers: ask DfE when the NI scheme opens and on what terms, and put the question to Assembly candidates.
source_title: Budget 2026, HC 726, paras 4.145 and 6.31 (HM Treasury, 28 October 2026)
note: GOV.UK's NI Budget release of 28 October 2026 gives no start date for the NI version.

title: Zero VAT on installed heat pumps and other energy-saving materials ends
detail: The zero rate on installing energy-saving materials in homes, heat pumps included, runs UK-wide (NI since 1 May 2023) until 31 March 2027. From 1 April 2027 they are reduced-rated, and heat batteries join the list.
action: Installers and housing providers: complete contracted installs before 1 April or price in the reduced rate.
source_title: VENSAV2083: VAT rates for energy-saving materials with commencement dates (HMRC manual)
note: Heat batteries added to the reduced rate from 1 April 2027 by Budget 2026 (para 6.215).

title: Plastic Packaging Tax: mass balance allowed, pre-consumer plastic excluded
detail: Chemically recycled plastic can count as recycled content using a mass balance approach, and pre-consumer plastic no longer counts towards the 30% recycled content threshold.
action: Check whether your recycled-content claims rely on pre-consumer scrap; if so, re-test against the 30% threshold.
source_title: Plastic Packaging Tax: mass balance approach and removal of pre-consumer plastic (HMRC policy paper)
note: Plastic Packaging Tax applies UK-wide.

title: Landfill tax 2027–28 rates take effect
detail: The standard rate rises with RPI and the lower rate by the same cash amount (Budget 2026). The Landfill Communities Fund credit cap rises from 5.3% to 8.3%. Landfill tax applies in England and Northern Ireland.
sectors: Councils; Waste and recycling; Construction and developers
action: Councils and contractors: update 2027–28 disposal budgets and gate fees.
source_title: Landfill Communities Fund value 2027 to 2028 (HMRC, 28 October 2026)
note: Rate uprating from Budget 2026, HC 726, para 6.221.

title: Zero emission company car tax rises to 5%
detail: The benefit-in-kind appropriate percentage for zero emission company cars is 5% for 2027–28, up from 4%.
action: Fleet managers: reflect the new rate in salary sacrifice and car policy quotes.
source_title: Taxation of company cars: appropriate percentage for 2025–26 to 2027–28 (HMRC policy paper)
note: The policy paper gives 5% for zero emission cars in 2027–28 in its summary; its detailed table quotes only the overall maximum.

title: NI Assembly and council elections
detail: Combined Assembly and local government elections. The new Executive and councils set the next Climate Action Plan, contaminated land, water funding and energy support decisions.
action: Put your asks to parties before manifestos close, early in 2027.
source_title: Local Government Elections 2027 (Causeway Coast and Glens Borough Council report, 28 April 2026, citing the Secretary of State)

title: Soil Nutrient Health Scheme deadline for the Farm Sustainability Payment
detail: Farms must complete Soil Nutrient Health Scheme registration and training by the close of the 2027 single application window, or lose 10% of the Farm Sustainability Payment in 2027, rising to 15% in 2028.
action: Register and book training well before 15 May.
source_title: Farm Sustainability Payment conditionalities (DAERA, 23 February 2026)

title: Draft determination for NI Water's PC28 price control
detail: The Utility Regulator publishes its draft determination for 2028–2033 for consultation.
sectors: Councils; Construction and developers; Water customers
action: Respond on wastewater capacity in your area; this sets what is built to 2033.
source_title: Decision published on approach to PC28, NI Water's next price control (Utility Regulator)

title: EU deforestation rules reach micro and small firms
detail: Micro and small operators placing cattle, cocoa, coffee, palm oil, rubber or soya products on the NI market must comply. Wood products were already covered from 30 December 2026.
sectors: Food and drink; Retail and hospitality; Importers
action: Smaller cafés, bakeries and processors: ask suppliers whether they are the first placer and who files the due diligence statement.
source_title: Moving, exporting or placing deforestation-free products on the market in Northern Ireland (GOV.UK, updated 27 August 2026)

title: GB zero VAT on household electricity due to end; NI stays at 5%
detail: The temporary zero rate on domestic electricity in Great Britain, which began on 1 October 2026, was extended by the Budget to 1 July 2027. It has never applied in NI, where qualifying supplies stay at the reduced 5% rate.
action: Watch for any further extension or comparable NI support; none was announced for NI households in the Budget.
source_title: Budget 2026, HC 726, para 6.210 (HM Treasury, 28 October 2026)
note: HMRC's GB guidance (updated 30 September 2026) still shows the original end date of 31 March 2027. Some site posts say 30 June 2027; the Budget text says 'to 1 July 2027'.

title: Fuel duty 5p cut and freeze end
detail: The temporary 5p a litre fuel duty cut and the freeze run to 1 July 2027 (red diesel included), after which rates step up.
sectors: Transport and shipping; Farmers; Construction and developers; Fleet operators
action: Hauliers and contractors: build the July step into contract fuel clauses and quotes running past mid-2027.
source_title: Budget 2026, HC 726, para 6.211 (HM Treasury, 28 October 2026)
note: GOV.UK's NI Budget release says the cut is extended to 30 June 2027.

title: Battery due diligence duties enforceable
detail: Under the EU Batteries Regulation in NI, economic operators in scope must have supply-chain due diligence policies for battery raw materials. The thresholds may change.
action: If you place batteries on the NI market above the turnover threshold, draft your due diligence policy and get it verified.
source_title: EU batteries regulations in Northern Ireland (GOV.UK, updated 17 October 2026)

title: First EU CBAM annual declaration and surrender
detail: EU importers declare embedded emissions in goods imported during 2026 and surrender CBAM certificates.
action: Expect EU customers' final data requests over the summer; send verified actual emissions to replace default values.
source_title: CBAM certificates (Environmental Protection Agency, Ireland)
note: The EU CBAM does not apply in NI.

title: Deposit return scheme goes live
detail: Single-use PET plastic, steel and aluminium drinks containers from 150ml to 3 litres carry a deposit in NI and England, run by UK Deposit Management Organisation Ltd, which sets the deposit.
sectors: Food and drink; Retail and hospitality; Packaging producers; Councils
action: Drinks producers: register with the UK DMO and change labels. Shops: plan return points or check whether you qualify for an exemption.
source_title: Extended Producer Responsibility: deposit return scheme for single-use drinks containers (DAERA, updated 14 April 2026)
note: DAERA gives October 2027 without a day.

title: Digital waste tracking extends to carriers, brokers and dealers
detail: Phase 2 of the digital waste tracking service is expected to become mandatory for waste carriers, brokers and dealers, after a public beta from April 2027.
sectors: Waste and recycling; Councils; Construction and developers
action: Carriers and brokers: join the April 2027 beta; producers: ask your carrier how it will record your loads.
source_title: Digital waste tracking (NetRegs, for NIEA and SEPA)
note: NetRegs and GOV.UK (updated 1 October 2026) both give October 2027.

title: PFHxA ban extends to other consumer textiles and leather
detail: The EU REACH restriction on PFHxA and related substances (entry 79), which applies in NI, covers textiles, leather, furs and hides for the general public other than clothing from 10 October 2027. Clothing, footwear and paper food packaging were covered from 10 October 2026.
action: Retailers and upholsterers: get PFHxA-free declarations for soft furnishings, outdoor textiles and leather goods sold in NI.
source_title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/2462 (EUR-Lex)
note: Dates read in the Official Journal text of the regulation.

title: ESOS phase 4 notification deadline
detail: Qualifying undertakings notify compliance with phase 4. NIEA is the regulator for organisations registered in NI.
action: Have the audit signed off by a lead assessor and the board in time to notify by 5 December.
source_title: How to comply with ESOS phase 4 (GOV.UK, published 30 July 2026)

title: EU Forced Labour Regulation would apply in NI
detail: If the Joint Committee adds Regulation (EU) 2024/3015 to the Windsor Framework, products made with forced labour could not be placed on the NI market or exported from it from 14 December 2027. GB would have its own regime for businesses with turnover over £350 million.
action: Map high-risk inputs (cotton, solar components, electronics, seafood) and supplier audits now.
source_title: Explanatory memorandum on Regulation (EU) 2024/3015 (UK Government, 4 November 2026)
note: Depends on the Joint Committee decision expected on 10 November 2026.

title: NI's first carbon budget period ends
detail: The first budgetary period under the Climate Change Act (Northern Ireland) 2022 runs from 2023 to 2027, with an average annual emissions reduction of 33%.
action: Public bodies: align 2027–28 plans with the second budget, which starts the next day.
source_title: Climate Change Act (Northern Ireland) 2022, Part 2 (legislation.gov.uk)
note: Budget level from DAERA's news release of 11 December 2024 on the Climate Change (Carbon Budgets 2023–2037) Regulations (NI) 2024.

title: Final determination for NI Water's PC28 price control
detail: The Utility Regulator intends to publish its final determination for 2028–2033.
sectors: Councils; Construction and developers; Water customers
action: Check which wastewater schemes are funded before committing to sites that need new connections.
source_title: Decision published on approach to PC28, NI Water's next price control (Utility Regulator)

title: NI's second carbon budget period starts
detail: The second budgetary period runs from 2028 to 2032, with an average annual emissions reduction of 48% set by the Climate Change (Carbon Budgets 2023–2037) Regulations (NI) 2024.
action: Expect the Climate Action Plan and sectoral plans for 2028–2032 to tighten what is asked of business and councils.
source_title: Muir welcomes Assembly approval of emissions targets (DAERA, 11 December 2024)

title: New EU chemical label format, advertising and online-sales rules apply
detail: Regulation (EU) 2025/2439 postponed parts of the CLP revision to 1 January 2028: label formatting, updating labels, advertising, distance (online) selling and labelling at fuel stations. CLP applies in NI.
sectors: Chemicals; Retail and hospitality; Farmers; Online sellers
action: Redesign labels and online listings for hazardous products sold in NI in time for 1 January 2028.
source_title: Regulation (EU) 2025/2439 amending the CLP revision's application dates (EUR-Lex)
note: Dates checked against a summary of the Official Journal text; the EUR-Lex page did not open from here.

title: HMRC opens UK CBAM registration
detail: Businesses whose covered imports passed £50,000 in 2027 register with HMRC.
action: Register as soon as it opens if you passed the threshold in 2027.
source_title: Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism: policy summary (HMRC, updated 2 November 2026)

title: Packaging data collection by nation starts in NI
detail: NIEA's regulatory position statement delays collection of nation data, and of self-managed organisational waste data, under the packaging EPR regulations to 1 January 2028. Nation data is reported by 1 April 2029.
sectors: Packaging producers; Retail and hospitality; Food and drink
action: Large packaging producers: set up systems to record where packaging is sold by nation from 1 January 2028.
source_title: Packaging EPR regulatory position statement (NIEA, September 2026)
note: NIEA will not normally take enforcement action before these dates; the legal duty is unchanged.

title: UK CBAM registration deadline for 2027
detail: Businesses that passed the £50,000 threshold during 2027 must register with HMRC by 31 January 2028.
action: Register by 31 January; late registration risks penalties.
source_title: Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism: policy summary (HMRC, updated 2 November 2026)

title: Low emission slurry spreading on farms over 100 livestock units
detail: DAERA's proposed Nutrients Action Programme 2027–2030 would make low emission slurry spreading equipment mandatory by February 2028 for farms over 100 livestock units, by February 2029 for farms over 75 units (and large pig units) and by February 2030 for farms over 50 units.
action: Larger farms: price trailing shoe or injection kit or contractor rates, and watch for capital grants.
source_title: Consultation on the Nutrients Action Programme 2027–2030, section 4.2.3 (DAERA, June 2026)
note: Consultation closed on 7 September 2026; the final programme was not published on 9 November 2026.

title: Carbon Price Support ends in Great Britain
detail: The government will end Carbon Price Support rates in Great Britain from April 2028. NI generators are in the EU ETS and do not pay it.
action: Expect GB wholesale power prices to fall relative to the all-island market; factor this into GB–NI site cost comparisons.
source_title: Budget 2026, HC 726, para 6.208 (HM Treasury, 28 October 2026)
note: The Budget says 'from April 2028' without a day; 1 April is the start of the levy year.

title: Climate Change Levy: electricity rate frozen, gas rate rises
detail: Electricity and LPG main rates are frozen at 2027–28 levels; gas and solid fuel main rates rise by RPI.
action: Use the widening gap between electricity and gas levy rates in the business case for electrifying heat.
source_title: Budget 2026, HC 726, para 6.209 (HM Treasury, 28 October 2026)

title: NI Water's PC28 price control period starts
detail: PC28 covers 1 April 2028 to 31 March 2033 and sets NI Water's funding and outputs, including wastewater capacity.
sectors: Councils; Construction and developers; Water customers
action: Developers and councils: plan development phasing around the funded capacity schemes.
source_title: Decision published on approach to PC28, NI Water's next price control (Utility Regulator)

title: Zero emission company car tax rises to 7%
detail: The appropriate percentage for zero emission company cars rises by 2 points a year in 2028–29 and 2029–30, from 5% to 7% on 6 April 2028.
action: Fleet managers: model whole-life cost with the higher rates before renewing leases that run past April 2028.
source_title: Taxation of company cars: appropriate percentage for 2028–29 and 2029–30 (HMRC policy paper)

title: First UK ETS surrender for domestic shipping
detail: Ship operators surrender allowances for 2026 and 2027 emissions together. Voyages between GB and NI, in either direction, get a 50% deduction while the price gap with Republic of Ireland routes remains.
sectors: Transport and shipping; Importers; Retail and hospitality
action: Freight buyers: check how ferry surcharges recover the 2026–27 cost and whether the 50% deduction is passed on.
source_title: UK ETS scope expansion: domestic maritime, main Authority response (GOV.UK)

title: Bovine Genetics deadline for the Farm Sustainability Payment
detail: Farms with cattle must complete Bovine Genetics Project registration and training by 15 May 2028, or lose 10% of the Farm Sustainability Payment in 2028, rising to 15% in 2029.
action: Register and complete training before the 2028 single application deadline.
source_title: Farm Sustainability Payment conditionalities (DAERA, 23 February 2026)

title: First UK CBAM return and payment
detail: Registered importers file their first UK CBAM return and pay for the 2027 accounting period, five months after it ends.
action: Reconcile 2027 import records and supplier emissions data in early 2028 so the return and payment are ready by 31 May.
source_title: Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism: policy summary (HMRC, updated 2 November 2026)

title: EU deadline to transpose the narrowed due diligence directive
detail: Member states must transpose the Omnibus I changes to the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive by 26 July 2028; companies apply it from 26 July 2029. In scope: EU groups over 5,000 employees and €1.5bn turnover. Not in the Windsor Framework, but NI suppliers to large EU groups will be asked about their supply chains.
sectors: Exporters to the EU; Manufacturers; Food and drink
action: Suppliers to large EU groups: expect codes of conduct and supplier questionnaires; keep human rights and environmental records ready.
source_title: Directive (EU) 2026/470 (Omnibus I), Official Journal, 26 February 2026 (EUR-Lex)
note: Transposition date read in the adopted text (Council PE-CONS 66/25, Article 5).

title: First self-managed packaging waste data report due in NI
